newsitem.title: USA: Niagara Mohawk sets accounting change.
newsitem.headline: Niagara Mohawk sets accounting change.

text.p: Niagara Mohawk Power Corp on Thursday said it took a charge against fourth-quarter earnings to reflect a writedown of regulatory assets required after its decision to change accounting.

With the charge, the utility's fourth quarter loss was $25.8 million, or $0.24 per share, the company said after a special board meeting where its directors declared dividends at prescribed rates for all series of preferred stock.
The special meeting followed Monday's announcement of an agreement in principle to terminate or restructure 44 independent power contracts.

"Our agreement in principle with independent power producers has clarified several important issues, allowing us to close our books for 1996 and declare preferred dividends," Chief Executive William E. Davis said.

The agreement allows the company to move forward with its PowerChoice initiative, in which the company has proposed to have its fossil and hydro-generating plants sell power in the competitive market, Niagara Mohawk said.
Accordingly, earnings for 1996 reflect the discontinued application of regulatory accounting principles in FAS 71 to the company's fossil and hydro generation business.
The discontinuance results in a write-off of $103.6 million of regulatory assets, resulting in an extraordinary loss after tax of $67.4 million, or $0.47 per share.
Excluding the extraordinary loss, earnings in 1996 were $139.5 million, or 97 cents per share, compared with 1995 earnings of $208.4 million, or $1.44 per share.

Niagara Mohawk said earnings declined last year because of an increase in bad debt expense of $96.4 million, with an earnings impact of $0.43 per share. That was partially offset by a $15 million gain in the fourth quarter on an asset sale, which contributed $0.10 per share to 1996 earnings.
Additionally, 1995 earnings included a one-time gains of about $24.5 million, or $0.17 per share.

Electric revenues for 1996 were $3.3 billion, a decrease of 0.8 percent from a year earlier, when revenues included a one-time $71.5 million unbilled, non-cash revenue amount authorized by its 1995 regulatory agreement.

The first-quarter dividend rate per annum for the adjustable rate preferred Series A stock is 6.50 percent; for Series B, 7.50 percent; and for Series C, 7.00 percent. Those rates equate to payments of $0.40625; $0.46875; and $0.4375 per share, respectively, payable March 31 to shareholders of record on March 20.
